title: Chlorine isotope puzzle
hook: Use the numbers to build the particle picture.

doesNotKnow: How to find neutron count from mass number.

objective: Calculate neutrons from atomic and mass numbers.

claims.text: Question, stage and reveal: A chlorine-35 atom has mass number 35 and atomic number 17. How many neutrons are in its nucleus? The nucleus has 17 protons and 18 neutrons. The mass number counts both: 17 + 18 = 35. The drawing is a counting model; nucleons are not arranged as a flat grid.
The drawing is schematic, not a spatial model of the nucleus.
Recall: An isotope has mass number 13 and atomic number 6. How many neutrons does it have? Mass number is protons plus neutrons, so 13 − 6 = 7.

recall.question: An isotope has mass number 13 and atomic number 6. How many neutrons does it have?
recall.why: Mass number is protons plus neutrons, so 13 − 6 = 7.
